Hi Marissa,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the demo and for walking through Redwood's routing/ autoscaling capabilities. As discussed, our team is ready to scope a 2-week POC to validate cost/latency targets and to exercise burst capacity under realistic traffic. A few quick context items from our side: 

- Expected baseline: ~1,000 LLM requests/day (mostly during business hours).
- Peak: bursts up to ~40 concurrent requests; some heavier batch jobs overnight.
- Typical prompt: ~600 input tokens, expected generated tokens ~350.
- Primary success criteria: 95th perc latency under 350ms for single-turn requests; cost per 1k tokens under $X (we can refine).

Can you send a short POC plan that includes: success criteria, what capacity you recommend (reserved GPUs vs. shared), autoscaling knobs/limits, and a proposed timeline? Also let me know owners on your side and any info you need from engineering/security.

Appreciate it — Jordan and I will review and loop in infra.

Thanks,
Kate Simmons
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme AI

Hi Kate (and Jordan),

Thanks — great meeting. Summary and proposed POC plan below. I kept this focused so your infra team can quickly validate the capacity asks.

POC objectives / success criteria
- Latency: 95th < 350ms for single-turn requests to the selected model under POC load.
- Throughput: handle baseline traffic (1k req/day) and sustain bursts to 40 concurrent requests without >5% error rate.
- Cost signal: measure end-to-end cost per 1k tokens during the POC; target <customer threshold — we'll work with you to set a target based on model choice.
- Functional: integrations (auth, request/response logging), and eval run on your prompt set with our eval harness.

Evaluation plan / timeline
- Week 0 (prep): share prompt set, keys, and sample load pattern (you) — by Jul 16.
- Week 1 (deploy + warm): reserve capacity, deploy model variant, warm KV/cache (Redwood) — Jul 20–24.
- Week 2 (stress + measure): run load tests and real traffic, collect metrics, iterate on autoscale values — Jul 27–31.
- Final review: joint review of metrics and next-step recommendations — Aug 3.

Ownership
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (sales/POC owner), Nikhil Sharma (solutions engineering, technical lead).
- Acme AI: Kate Simmons (platform lead), Jordan Lee (infra).

Capacity recommendation (initial)
- Reserved: 2 x dedicated GPUs (NVIDIA A100-40GB equiv) for the POC window to guarantee base throughput and reduce cold-start variability.
- Autoscale policy: min=1 instance (shared/dedicated hybrid), target CPU/GPU util 55–65%, scale step=+1 instance, cooldown=60s, max=6 instances for POC bursts.
- Burst behavior: allow temporary burst to Redwood shared pool up to 8 additional units for short periods (rate-limited) — recommend we set burst budget and alert thresholds.
- Caching: enable KV/prefix cache for repeated prompts; expect 10–20% token savings for typical Acme workload.

Attachments: I attached a compact capacity worksheet with estimated throughput numbers and an inference config sketch.

Next steps
1) Jordan: confirm you can share a representative prompt set and any load-test scripts by Jul 16.
2) Nikhil & I will finalize config + SOW draft and share the Drive link by Jul 12.
3) Schedule kickoff: propose Tue Jul 20 10am PT for an onboarding + infra alignment call.

If this looks reasonable I'll start the SOW draft and loop in pricing.

Best,

--
Marissa Cole

On Thu, Jul 9, 2026 at 11:08 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Capacity recommendation (initial)
> - Reserved: 2 x dedicated GPUs (NVIDIA A100-40GB equiv) for the POC window to guarantee base throughput and reduce cold-start variability.
> - Autoscale policy: min=1 instance (shared/dedicated hybrid), target CPU/GPU util 55–65%, scale step=+1 instance, cooldown=60s, max=6 instances for POC bursts.

Thanks — adding technical detail so your infra can validate: 

1) Baseline sizing rationale
- With your median prompt/generation sizes (~950 tokens total), a single A100-40GB instance (well-optimized model) can sustain ~10–14 concurrent low-latency requests depending on model variant and quantization. Conservatively, 2 reserved GPUs should cover baseline + moderate concurrency and reduce jitter from cold starts.

2) Autoscale + burst behavior
- For POC: use a hybrid pool (1 reserved instance + autoscale up to 5 dedicated instances). Reserve the second GPU as warm standby which can be fully dedicated or used as part of autoscale depending on your preference.
- Burst: configure policy to allow short-term spillover to Redwood shared capacity (budgeted) for spikes above max dedicated nodes. We'll enforce a burst rate limiter (e.g., max concurrency to shared pool = 8 nodes for 10 minutes).

3) Operational knobs we recommend for the POC
- KV cache TTL: 2 hours (for conversational reuse).
- Token limits: hard cap at 2,048 tokens per request to avoid OOMs; surface per-request token metrics to your dashboard.
- Batching: enable small batching window (10–15ms) to improve throughput; we will tune during week 1.

4) Failover & monitoring
- Set automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if tail latency exceeds thresholds.
- We will provide dashboards for per-route 95/99 latency, GPU util, queue length, token usage, and cost-per-token.

Attached is a minimal inference config you can drop into your infra automation. We'll iterate based on your perf runs.

- Nikhil
